question: You are a senior Venture Capital analyst. How would you currently rate the Qnami's execution's capabilities? As senior technologists with a track record have. a better chance of achieving engineering breakthroughs. Give a brutally honest score from 1–10 and a 200 word explanation.
answer:
Here’s my brutally honest assessment of Qnami’s execution capabilities, from the perspective of a senior VC analyst:

Score: 7 out of 10

Explanation (approx. 200 words):

Qnami has demonstrated solid execution in translating deep-tech quantum sensing into commercial products. Their ProteusQ, the first commercial scanning NV (nitrogen-vacancy) magnetometer, launched in 2019 and has gained traction in top-tier research institutions across Europe and North America ([qnami.ch](https://qnami.ch/qnami-closes-4-0m-chf-series-a-round/?utm_source=openai)). Strategic partnerships—such as with HORIBA for global distribution and Quantum Design for expansion into Japan and South Korea—underscore their ability to scale distribution effectively ([horiba.com](https://www.horiba.com/int/scientific/resources/news/detail/news/7/2020/horiba-signs-strategic-cooperation-agreement-with-qnami-to-accelerate-scanning-nv-magnetometry-deve/?utm_source=openai)).

Customer feedback is overwhelmingly positive, highlighting the ProteusQ’s stability, ease of use, and performance in demanding research environments ([qnami.ch](https://qnami.ch/?utm_source=openai)). More recently, Qnami has begun to move beyond academia into industrial applications, supporting semiconductor innovation through collaborations like the one with VerticalCompute ([qnami.ch](https://qnami.ch/qnami-supports-verticalcompute-driving-european-semiconductor-innovation/?utm_source=openai)).

However, there are areas for improvement. Their funding rounds—seed in 2019 and Series A in 2021—suggest a slower capital trajectory compared to high-growth deep-tech peers ([qnami.ch](https://qnami.ch/qnami-closes-2-6m-chf-seed-round/?utm_source=openai)). Additionally, while partnerships and product adoption are strong, broader commercial scale-up into manufacturing and industrial markets remains nascent.

In summary, Qnami shows strong technical execution and early commercial traction, but still has room to accelerate growth and scale.
